conventions.convention: Gaussian moments are initially two-sided improper Riemann integrals; gamma and beta parameters are strictly positive. Lebesgue consumers supply their own comparison and product-measure hypotheses.
The Jacobian is det(D_a χ_t), with χ_0 the identity. The supplied family is jointly C2 and consists of diffeomorphisms; no flow-existence result is asserted. Torus matrices use translation frames.
Fine entropy is the dimensionless quantity −∫f log f dμ relative to the fixed measure μ=c da; the initial density is C1 and bounded strictly above zero.

The continuous Lebesgue calculations explicitly assume Countable Choice. The spherical law is the specified Gaussian-direction construction P=RZ/|Z|, with P=0 on the null event Z=0; its density formula requires 1≤k<D.

Preparations are adopted probability laws. β=(k_B T)⁻¹; U, F and S have the stated statistical thermodynamic definitions. The action reference h_0=a_0>0 is fixed, with no identification with Planck's constant. Resolved harmonic coordinates omit particle-exchange factorials; indistinguishable particle models retain their declared factorials.

The ideal gas has one operationally indistinguishable species and reference dq dp/(N! h_0^(dN)). A one-particle marginal means a uniformly selected particle. The vacuum is a singleton of unit reference mass with H_0=0 and Z_0=1. The H=c|p| branch is separately adopted.

The periodic Ising ring counts exactly N indexed bonds, including two bonds when N=2; J≥0, β>0 and zero field are required for the displayed correlation formula. The correlation length is defined for the fixed-separation infinite-ring limit when J>0.
Hard rods have centers in [a/2,L−a/2], pair separation at least a, a≥0 and L>Na. The quantity p_1D is force conjugate to length, in newtons. The virial expansion and remainder require aρ<1.

load_bearing.statement: For a>0 and integer r≥0, I_r(a)=Γ(r+1/2)a^(−r−1/2), odd Gaussian moments vanish, and I_r′(a)=−I_(r+1)(a). For s,t>0, Γ(s)Γ(t)=Γ(s+t)B(s,t), Γ(s+1)=sΓ(s), and Γ(1/2)=√π. Independent unit-scale gamma variables convolve by adding their positive shape parameters.

Each named finite model adopts its explicitly stated preparation. Canonical probability is Z⁻¹e^(−βH)dν when β>0 and 0<Z<∞; grand-sector weights are z^N Z_N/Ξ. Thermodynamic definitions and the fixed action/counting conventions are adopted separately from dynamics or empirical realization.

Assuming Countable Choice, D≥2, 1≤k<D and R>0, P=RZ/|Z| for independent standard-normal coordinates is rotationally invariant and concentrated on |P|=R. Its first k coordinates have density Γ(D/2)/[Γ((D−k)/2)(πR²)^(k/2)] times (1−|y|²/R²)^((D−k−2)/2) for |y|<R, and zero otherwise. Coordinate variances are R²/D. With fixed k and R_D=√D σ, the block converges against every bounded Lipschitz test function to k independent centered Gaussians of variance σ².

Assuming Countable Choice, for symmetric positive-definite K∈R^(n×n), n≥1 and β>0, the full-space density proportional to exp(−βxᵀKx/2) has Z=(2π/β)^(n/2)(det K)^(−1/2), mean zero, covariance β⁻¹K⁻¹ and mean quadratic energy n/(2β).

Under the stated Countable Choice, box, one-species counting and canonical preparation hypotheses, Z_N=V^N/(N!λ^(dN)), including Z_0=1; momentum components are independent centered Gaussians of variance m/β, U=dN/(2β), Var(H_N)=dN/(2β²), and pressure satisfies PV=N/β. The grand count is Poisson with parameter zV/λ^d.

For the supplied jointly C2 diffeomorphic family with identity initial map and C1 velocity b, ∂_tF=(D_xb)(t,χ)F and ∂_tJ=J div b(t,χ), with J(0,a)=1 and J>0. If div b=0, J=1. The same identities hold in the stated flat-torus translation frames.

For the stated supplied incompressible smooth diffeomorphic flow on a flat torus and positive bounded C1 probability density f_0, f_t=f_0∘χ_t⁻¹ remains normalized, and its finite dimensionless fine entropy satisfies H(f_t)=H(f_0).

For the stated zero-field periodic indexed-bond ring, N≥2, J≥0 and β>0, t=tanh(βJ)∈[0,1), the one-site mean is zero and E[s_i s_(i+r)]=(t^r+t^(N−r))/(1+t^N) for 1≤r<N. At fixed positive r the limit is t^r; for J>0 its correlation length is −1/log t.

Under the stated Countable Choice and hard-rod canonical hypotheses, Z_N=(L−Na)^N/(N!λ^N), U=N/(2β), and βp_1D=ρ/(1−aρ). For aρ<1 this equals the convergent virial series; after M≥1 terms its exact remainder is ρ(aρ)^M/(1−aρ).

The stated finite Gaussian-direction shell preparation has total energy E almost surely and variance zero. The separate canonical ideal gas at β=D/(2E) has the same mean and positive energy variance. For N>1 its selected-particle Gaussian momentum has positive tails outside the compact support of the shell marginal.

concerns.concern: The title says “Exact finite-ring correlation length at a chosen coupling,” but the Example obtains ξ=1/log 3 from the fixed-r, N→∞ limit. Its supplier explicitly defines ξ as the limiting correlation length; the finite-ring correlation includes the additional 3^(−(N−r)) term. The body is correct, but the title should identify the limiting correlation length or the finite-ring correlations.

The Tong reference is labelled “§§2.2–2.2.4, ideal gas and Maxwell speed distribution.” Maxwell Distribution is §2.3, whereas §2.2.4 concerns the grand canonical ideal gas. The author's chapter contents and Maxwell formulas confirm the locator mismatch: [Tong, Classical Gases](https://davidtong.org/teaching/statistical-physics/statmechhtml/S2). The example's calculations are supported locally by its theorem.
